version: Flutter 3.47.8 (framework 737ba8f885, engine cf636b1dfb), Dart 3.13.7, package:ffi 2.2.0, Skia-GL
notes: Flutter Dart-AOT release, Linux GTK3 embedder, renderer: Skia (OpenGL), via fl_dart_project_set_enable_impeller(FALSE), GL = Mesa (llvmpipe under Xvfb). frame_ms = interval between consecutive FrameTiming rasterFinish timestamps (SchedulerBinding.addTimingsCallback; raster thread finished the frame and handed it to the GTK GL compositor; latest public post-render signal, not an X11 present timestamp). Only frames the engine rasterized are counted (Flutter produces no frame when nothing is dirty; every animated frame changes content). Pacing (BENCH_PACING, requested=60): native Flutter cadence = Ticker/SchedulerBinding frames driven by the engine vsync; the Linux GTK embedder registers no vsync callback, so the engine uses its fallback vsync waiter with a fixed 1/60 s tick (engine source shell/common/vsync_waiter_fallback.cc). No public/documented API uncaps it, so uncapped -> pacing "60-only". gc = null: Dart exposes no GC counters in AOT release. Warm-up 2 s; script time frozen at 0 during warm-up. text: Flutter has no virtualized single big text view; the file is split into lines (ListView.builder of Text) inside SelectableRegion. time_to_first_display_ms = main() entry -> rasterFinish of the first frame that built the text (excludes engine/VM startup before main). layout_ms = file read+split + buildDuration of that first frame (Flutter lays out lazily, only the viewport). Scroll = triangle wave 0..15000 px at 3000 px/s. Select-all at t=5 s via SelectableRegionState.selectAll(): with a lazy list only built lines are selected.
